chunks: Mūsā ibn Bakr narrated from al-ʿAbd al-Ṣāliḥ عليه السلام:
Regarding a man who struck another man with a stick and did not lift the stick from him until he died,

He عليه السلام said: “He is to be handed over to the heirs of the slain, but he is not to be left so that pleasure may be taken in torturing him; rather, retribution is to be carried out against him by the sword.”

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءِ الْمَقْتُولِ: the legal heirs of the person killed, who hold the right of retaliation
key_terms.الْمَقْتُولِ: the slain person, the victim of the killing
key_terms.بِالسَّيْفِ: with the sword, meaning formal execution in retaliation
key_terms.يُتَلَذَّذُ بِهِ: to take pleasure in inflicting suffering upon him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone beats a man with a stick until he dies?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a fatal beating with a stick. The killer is handed over to the heirs of the murdered person for retribution, but mutilation or torturous retaliation is prohibited; instead, execution is to be carried out with the sword.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5278 - Musa ibn Bakr narrated from Al-Abd Al-Salih Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim (as)
regarding a man who struck another man with a stick and did not lift it from him until he died.

Imam (as) said: "The killer should be handed over to the heirs of the murdered man, but he should not be left to be tortured for pleasure. Rather, retribution should be carried out upon him with the sword."
